correctness.rationale: For any FIXED prime p, multiplicativity of sigma gives f_p(n)=sum_{q^a||n}g_p(q,a), g_p=v_p(1+q+...+q^a). Let F_p(n)=sum_{q|n}v_p(q+1), a strongly additive proxy. For a>=2, g_p(q,a)+v_p(q+1) <= a log_p q+log_p(a+1)+log_p(q+1); weighted by q^-a, these terms are summable, giving mean absolute error O_p(1) and hence o(loglog x) outside density o(1). For q!=p, v_p(q+1)=sum_{j>=1}1_(q=-1 mod p^j); for q=p the term vanishes. Fixed-progression Mertens estimates, with the high-modulus tail controlled by Brun–Titchmarsh and direct sparse counting, give mean A_p(x)=sum_{q<=x}v_p(q+1)/q=(sum_{j>=1}1/phi(p^j)+o(1))loglog x = (p/(p-1)^2+o(1))loglog x. The second-moment proxy sum_{q<=x}v_p(q+1)^2/q=O_p(loglog x), since a_q²=sum_{j<=a_q}(2j-1) and sum j/phi(p^j) converges. Turán–Kubilius then yields mean square deviation O_p(x loglog x); Chebyshev and the bounded error transfer give f_p(n)~[p/(p-1)^2]loglog n in natural density. No finite experiment is treated as the proof. Independently checked finite n comparisons of the additive proxy and valuation (not an asymptotic certification).
